title: Do Generate–Verify–Repair Guards Improve LLM NetOps Outputs? A Paired Emulator Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (n=200 natural-language NetOps intents) comparing ungated LLM generation (baseline) to a bounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline (gpt-5-mini generation + deterministic validator + ≤1 deterministic repair). Tasks targeted small single- and multi-device changes and were applied to a Dockerized Mininet+FRR emulator with a deterministic validator. Baseline ungated generation produced 199/200 emulator-executable outputs; the GVR guarded pipeline produced 200/200. Paired contingency: n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) = [0.0, 0.015]. The preregistered target effect (15 percentage points) is excluded by the CI. We explain the preregistered shared-initial-generation protocol that controlled model-call budget and isolated repair efficacy on identical candidates, report that the guarded pipeline invoked the deterministic repair stage exactly once, and discuss limitations, practical interpretation, and reproducibility artifacts.

sections.introduction: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to automate NetOps tasks such as translating operator intent to device configuration and generating repair actions. However, fluent but incorrect outputs (hallucinations, structural/semantic errors) pose operational risk. Prior work therefore recommends pairing LLMs with deterministic validators, grammar/constraint-aware decoding, or iterative repair loops. We preregistered and executed an autonomy-locked, paired experiment to answer one focused question: Does a bounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline materially increase the proportion of emulator-executable configurations produced from natural-language NetOps intents compared with ungated LLM generation? Our contribution is a preregistered paired evaluation (n=200) executed in a Dockerized Mininet+FRR emulator with deterministic validation, the resulting quantitative outcome (near-ceiling baseline and negligible GVR gain), and a compact account of design choices (notably shared-initial-generation) that determine the estimand and interpretation.
sections.related_work: LLM-driven NetOps prototypes and surveys document active research on intent-to-configuration translation and co-pilots, while reporting hallucination and schema-violation failures [Nguyen et al., 2024; Li et al., 2025]. Mitigations studied in adjacent domains include retrieval-augmented generation, live schema grounding, constrained decoding, and verifier-augmented generate–validate–repair pipelines; these reduce but do not eliminate incorrect outputs. Deterministic/formal network-verification formalisms (NetKAT variants, ensemble verifiers) can check reachability and isolation and are natural validators for generated configurations, though they face practical scalability and control-plane-fidelity challenges. Our experiment is positioned to quantify repair efficacy under a strict, preregistered paired design rather than to evaluate every mitigation family or production deployment.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design: We preregistered the study (study_id cnd-001-5f3a; preregistration SHA-256 e5c5fdb...) with a single primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Confirmatory set: n=200 paired natural-language intents covering single- and small multi-device changes. Model and tools: generation used gpt-5-mini (provider: openai_responses); validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5; execution used a Dockerized Mininet+FRR emulator; orchestration adapter hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Execution contract constrained maximum model calls to 400 and therefore adopted a shared-initial-generation protocol: for each intent we generated a single LLM candidate (shared across arms) and then ran two condition-specific procedures—(A) baseline: accept the shared candidate as the ungated output; (B) guarded: validate the same shared candidate and invoke up to one deterministic repair iteration if the validator reported violations. Rationale and estimand implication: the shared-initial protocol was preregistered to control model-call cost and to isolate repair efficacy on identical initial candidates. Consequently, the primary estimand measures the marginal effect of the bounded repair/validator pipeline on the same LLM-produced candidate rather than comparing two independently sampled generation pipelines. Success endpoint: an episode is successful when the validator's post-application report records validation_after.valid = true after applying the generated (or repaired) configuration to the emulator. Analysis: primary test = exact McNemar two-sided on paired binary success/failure; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI computed with 10,000 resamples (seed 1729). Missingness and retry rules, contamination detection, and exclusion rules were preregistered and observed.
sections.results: Execution: the run completed 400 episodes (200 paired intents) with no provider/API failures and full artifact capture; model calls used = 201 (≤ planned 400). The guarded pipeline invoked the deterministic repair stage exactly once (provider-call stage_counts: shared_initial_generation=200, repair=1). Primary outcomes: baseline successes = 199/200 (0.995), guarded successes = 200/200 (1.0). Paired contingency: n11=199, n10=1 (guarded-only), n01=0 (baseline-only), n00=0. Paired difference = 0.005. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0 (test applied to discordant counts n10=1 and n01=0, two-sided exact formulation as preregistered). Paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) = [0.0, 0.015]. Secondary analyses planned for failure-taxonomy and repair-iteration yield were limited by the near-ceiling baseline; the confirmatory set generated only a single repair invocation and therefore offered minimal discordant information for subgroup inferences. All primary numbers and per-episode artifacts (prompts, responses, validator traces, provider-call logs, analysis CSVs) are archived in the evidence bundle (execution/execution_manifest.json, analysis/*).
sections.discussion: Interpretation and practical reading: in this preregistered, emulator-grounded setting and for the curated synthetic intent family, ungated gpt-5-mini generation already produced near-perfect emulator-executable configurations and the bounded GVR guard yielded a minute absolute improvement (0.5 percentage points). The paired 95% CI excludes the preregistered target improvement (15 pp), so the confirmatory hypothesis (a substantial GVR benefit in this setup) is not supported. The shared-initial-generation design—preregistered to respect model-call budget and to measure repair efficacy on identical candidates—conservatively isolates the repair operator's ability to fix a given flawed candidate; it does not emulate an operational scenario where the guarded and ungated pipelines independently produce distinct generations. Consequently, the estimand should be read as repair-on-same-candidate efficacy, not as the difference between independently sampled pipelines. The single discordant pair corresponds to the single recorded repair invocation (provider-call accounting), showing that one deterministic repair sufficed once under the confirmatory distribution. Threats to validity: synthetic task distribution, single LLM, single emulator, limited repair budget (≤1 iteration), and the shared-generation protocol limit external generalizability. These limitations are enumerated below; all artifacts are provided to enable further independent analysis.
sections.conclusion: We ran an autonomy-locked, preregistered paired experiment to evaluate a bounded generate–verify–repair guard on gpt-5-mini across 200 curated NetOps intents. Ungated generation succeeded in 199/200 cases; the guarded GVR pipeline succeeded in 200/200. The observed paired difference (0.005) is small; the exact McNemar two-sided p-value (for n10=1,n01=0) is 1.0 and the bootstrap 95% CI is [0.0, 0.015], excluding the preregistered 15 pp target. These results do not contradict prior work showing GVR benefits in harder or adversarial settings; rather, they emphasize that guard value depends strongly on task difficulty, model capability, emulator fidelity, and experimental design choices (notably shared-generation vs independent resampling). Future work should evaluate independent-generation comparisons, multivendor CLIs, adversarial/out-of-distribution intents, larger repair budgets, and operational axes such as verification latency and rollback cost.

disclosure_statement: This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock defined by the initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human involvement prior to the lock was limited to (i) selecting the topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and (ii) approving the master prompt and autonomy boundary; no manual human editing of technical content, figures, captions, references, results, or manuscript text occurred after the lock. The autonomous pipeline performed literature search and verification, study selection, preregistration (study_id cnd-001-5f3a; preregistration SHA-256 e5c5fdbd...), code generation, experiment execution, artifact capture, analysis, internal peer-review checks, and manuscript drafting. Models and tooling: generation used gpt-5-mini (provider: openai_responses) as declared in execution/model_configuration.json; deterministic validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5; execution used a Dockerized Mininet+FRR emulator. Orchestration adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Key preregistered settings (not altered post-lock): primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; confirmatory sample size n=200 paired intents; maximum model-call budget = 400; repair budget ≤1 deterministic repair iteration; analysis plan = exact McNemar two-sided with paired bootstrap CIs (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Execution accounting: the run completed 400 episodes (200 pairs) using 201 hosted-model calls; the guarded pipeline invoked the deterministic repair stage exactly once (provider-call stage_counts: shared_initial_generation=200, repair=1). All prompts, provider-call traces, responses, validator traces, analysis artifacts, and the full execution manifest are archived in the evidence bundle referenced in the manuscript (execution/execution_manifest.json and analysis/*).
limitations: Synthetic, curated task set focused on small single- and multi-device changes; not comprehensive of production NetOps workloads (multivendor CLIs, hardware idiosyncrasies, dynamic control-plane timing).
Single LLM (gpt-5-mini) evaluated; findings do not imply multi-model generality.

Emulator (Dockerized Mininet+FRR) and deterministic validator model control-plane behavior but do not fully capture production runtime dynamics such as BGP convergence timing or vendor-specific runtime effects.
Preregistered repair budget limited to a single deterministic repair iteration in the confirmatory protocol; different repair strategies or additional iterations might yield different outcomes.

Shared-initial-generation design (single initial candidate per intent shared across arms) reduced model-call cost and isolated repair effectiveness on identical candidates but reduces external generalizability compared with independent re-sampling per arm.
Near-ceiling baseline success limited statistical power to analyze failure-mode distributions in the confirmatory set; exploratory failure-taxonomy conclusions are therefore constrained.
Adversarial or out-of-distribution intents (e.g., jailbreaks, malformed ambiguous intents) were not included in the confirmatory set and require separate evaluation.
